newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kobe Steel to invest 158 bln yen in power project.
newsitem.headline: Kobe Steel to invest 158 bln yen in power project.

text.p: Kobe Steel Ltd said on Monday it would spend about 158 billion yen to build power generating facilities which will supply electricity to Kansai Electric Power Co Inc.
Kobe Steel said in a statement that it was awarded a contract to supply electricity to Kansai Electric on Monday.
It said the electricity would be generated at the Kobe and Kakogawa Works of Kobe Steel, both in Hyogo Prefecture, western Japan.
At the Kobe Works, Kobe Steel plans to spend about 150 billion yen to build a coal-burning power plant with a capacity of 700,000 kilowatts.
When the power plant starts operation in April 2002, it will supply 659,000 kilowatts to Kansai Electric, it said.
The Kakogawa Works would supply electricity to Kansai Electric from April 1999, using recycled heat, Kobe Steel said.
It said it would invest about eight billion yen to start electric power supply from Kakogawa.
The power plant would have a capacity of 58,000 kilowatts and supply 54,500 kilowatts to Kansai Electric, it said.
Kobe Steel said that in future it planned to build an additional 700,000-kilowatt power plant.
